Ins. Co. Ltd (hereinafter called R- 2) and vehicle no. DL 3SDX 4568 make Royal Enfield (hereinafter referred as accidental vehicle).
Brief Facts:
2. Preliminary information regarding accident in question was received at PS Sarita Vihar recorded vide DD No. 6A dated 17.03.2019, upon receipt of which, IO along with Ct. Jitender reached at place of accident which was in front of Nexa Showroom, near Aali Red Light, Mathura Road, New Delhi (hereinafter referred as spot of accident) where they found one motorcycle bearing registration number DL 3SDX 4568 & one Eicher Truck HR 74A 7880 in accidental condition. They came to know that injured persons had already been removed to hospital. Thereafter, they reached to Apollo Hospital and received MLC of MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 2 of 31 Apoorva Shuka with alleged history of "RTA injured declared brought dead" and MLC of injured Ankur Kushwaha with alleged history of "RTA nature of injury opinion reserved". Injured Ankur Kushwaha, however, showed inability to give statement to IO due to severe pain and ongoing treatment. IO again reached the spot and searched for eye witness and whether any CCTV were installed at the spot. Having not been able to locate any eye witness, FIR no. 100/2019 was registered on the basis of information received vide DD no. 6A and MLCs of injured persons. Both the accidental vehicles were taken into police possession. Post Mortem of deceased Apoorva Shukla was conducted. Mechanical Inspection of both the vehicles were got conducted by IO. Notice u/s 133 MV Act was served to driver Sadiq upon receipt of which he produced relevant documents of offending vehicle and stated that he is also the owner of the offending vehicle. 
3. Statement of injured Ankur Kushwaha was recorded by IO wherein he stated that he was pillion rider on accidental motorcycle driven by his friend Apoorv Shukla in the night of 16.03.2019-17.03.2019 at about 01.00 AM. It suddenly smashed against offending vehicle stationed in the middle of the road. 
4. IO then recorded statement of ASI Kulbir Singh who stated that in the night of 16-17.03.2019, he was on emergency duty and at about 12:00 midnight, upon receipt of DD no. 5A regarding accident,
he along with HC Dalchand reached near Nexa Showroom where they found that the aforesaid Eicher Truck was stationed having been damaged from both front and back side. 
MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 3 of 31 ASI Kulbir Singh asked the driver of such vehicle to park his vehicle on the side of the road. But he could not do so. He also asked him to pull the truck with the help of crane to the side of the road but driver of such Eicher Truck could not make any efforts. Even he did not put any reflector or parking light despite instruction. Thereafter,
ASI himself called control room for availability of crane. He also recorded statement of driver of such Eicher Truck and got registered FIR no.99/2019 u/s 279 IPC. He thereafter tried to divert Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
2 other vehicles plying on the road but unfortunately a Royal Enfiled DL 3SDX 4568, came from Sarita Vihar side and smashed into the Truck due to which the driver of motorcycle fell down on the road and the pillion rider was thrown in the air towards divider. He further gave information of such accident to police control room and send the injured persons to Apollo Hospital. He also got the truck removed from the road. 
5. IO also examined driver of Eicher Truck and recording his submissions, who specified that incident took place at 02.00 AM when he was stuck in the jam near Nexa Showroom, Aali Red Light. 
6. The driver of offending truck was arrested by IO after examination. Driver of Eicher Truck was produced before Criminal Court where he refused to participate in TIP proceedings. Relevant documents of such Eicher Truck taken into possession. MLC of Injured Ankur Kushwaha was obtained wherein nature of injury opined to be grievous. Upon completion of investigation,
charge-sheet was filed under Sections 279/338/304A IPC against driver and DAR was filed by MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 4 of 31 Investigating Officer before this Tribunal. 
Proceedings:
7. All the contesting parties appeared before the court. Copy of DAR was supplied to them. Reply to DAR was not filed by R- 1/ driver cum owner. Insurance Company, however filed its reply. 
Reply: 
8. In reply filed by Insurance Company, it is stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of another truck which was driven away after committing accident and no details of other truck have been provided by IO which actually committed the accident. It is stated that the other truck bearing Reg. no. HR 46D 7387, standing ahead of Eicher Truck bearing Reg. no. HR 74A 7880 was also lying in accidental condition but there is no mentioning of such truck in the DAR. It is stated that the present DAR is bad for mis-joinder & non-joinder of necessary parties. It is stated that the victims were themselves negligent as they collided with the truck at the time when ASI Kulbir Singh was diverting the traffic plying on the road which itself affirm that the accident was caused by another truck who details has not been furnished by IO. It is stated that there are 3 trucks involved, however, registration number of only two trucks, has been mentioned. However, it is admitted that the alleged Eicher Truck was insured with the answering insurance company. Other general defences were taken. 
9. From the pleadings of parties, following issues were MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . 
Page No. 5 of 31 framed vide order dated 29.10.2020:
i). Whether the deceased Gauri Shukla suffered fatal injuries in a road traffic accident on 17.03.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle HR 74A 7880 being driven & Owned by R-1 and insured with R-2? OPP. 
Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
3 ii). Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP iii). Relief. 
10. Perusal of Issue no.1 reflects that there is wrong mentioning of name of victim. To avoid any confusion, issue no.1 is reframed as under:
Whether the injured Ankur Kushwaha suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 17.03.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle HR 74A 7880 being driven &
Owned by R-1 and insured with R-2? OPP. 
Evidence:
11. Thereafter matter was listed for recording of evidence of petitioner. 
12. Injured victim Sh. Ankur Kushwaha stepped in the witness box as PW2 in the connected matter titled as "Gauri Shukla & Ors. Vs. Saddiq & Ors" who tendered her affidavit in evidence as Ex.PW2/A and relied upon copy of his Aadhar Card as Ex.PW1/1.
13. He was then cross examined by counsel for insurance MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr.
. Page No. 6 of 31 company. 
14. PE was then closed vide order dated 21.09.2022. Matter was listed for RE, however, no RE led by any of the respondents. 
15. Final Submissions were advanced by counsel for claimants as well as respondents. Counsel for claimant has argued that the insurance company has not taken any statutory defence and that any of the respondent have not adduced any evidence. He has further argued that eye witness has clearly deposed about the negligence on the part of R-1 which led to the accident. He has prayed that compensation be awarded to LRs of deceased as per applicable provisions of law. Counsel for insurance company has fairly conceded that there is no statutory defence and the matter may be decided as per law. She however stated that bikes rammed into stationary truck which reflects upon negligence in causing upon their own negligence in causing the accident. 
16. On the basis of material on record as no evidence has been adduced in the matter, issue wise findings are as under :
Issue No.1 Whether the injured Ankur Kushwaha suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 17.03.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle HR 74A 7880 being driven & Owned by R-1 and insured with R-2? OPP. 
17. It is well settled that the proceedings before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of inquiry and the finding of rash and negligent driving by driver of the offending vehicle is to be MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
4 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 7 of 31 returned only at the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities. The factors noted above are sufficient to conclude that preponderance of probability is made out showing negligence of respondent no.1 in causing the accident. 
18. Police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under Section 279/338/304 A IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent no.1 in causing the accident. Certified copy of charge sheet was also filed before this Court. In National Insurance Co.
Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet under relevant section are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 
19. It is also settled that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him as observed by Hon'ble High Court of India in the case of Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310. In the present case also, driver did not enter into the witness box to controvert the claim of petitioner or even to explain circumstances of accident. More so, he never filed reply and never contested the petition. 
20. Claimant Ankur Kushwaha appeared as eye witness in the connected matter titled as Gauri Shukla Vs. Sadiq. He deposed that the accidental motorcycle collided with the stationary truck,
illegally parked in the middle of the road without any indicator, reflector or any other precaution. 
He was extensively cross examined by counsel for insurance company. He clarified therein that he was not driving the vehicle and was sitting as a pillion MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. .
Page No. 8 of 31 rider which was driven by his deceased friend Apoorv at the time of accident and both of them were wearing helmets at the time of accident. He also clarified that there was no street light on the spot of accident and that it was absolutely dark on the road. He also stated that there was no traffic on the road at the time of accident. He also clarified that he happened to spot the alleged offending vehicle only 10 seconds prior to the accident and that he lost consciousness immediately after the accident. However, regained consciousness after few minutes when he found himself lying on the kaccha side of the road while the accidental vehicle and his deceased friend were spotted lying behind the truck. He also stated that the truck was parked in the middle of the road, however, there was sufficient space for bike to pass on the left side of the truck through which a car could also pass as compared to the right side of the truck with trees and plantation on the divider of the road. He also stated that the bike was being driven at speed of 35-40 kmph at the time of accident. 
21. What can be understood is that the alleged offending vehicle was stationed at about middle of the road in late night hours with no visibility (no street lights as per evidence) which could not be spotted from a distance enabling the rider of the bike to apply brakes to avert the accident. As per the proceedings in the charge sheet, this offending vehicle itself met with an accident few hours earlier with another vehicle, qua which a separate FIR bearing no. 99/2019, PS Sarita Vihar has been registered. The contents of the complaint which was made the basis for registration of FIR no.
99/2019 note that this offending MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 9 of 31 vehicle was hit by another truck because of which in turn, it rammed into yet another truck and its body therefore got damaged from the front as well as back side. Same is found mentioned as such in Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
5 the seizure memo which also notes that it ignition capacity was found incapacitated. Mechanical Inspection Report also notes damage on the front and rear side and certified the vehicle to be "off road condition".
22. The point of examination remains as to the duration the gap between earlier accident and the subsequent event in question and whether intimation in respect of the earlier accident was promptly given to the authority concerned including police officials and whether any effort was made to remove the truck at least one side of the road or altogether from the road or at least to take some measure in the meanwhile to indicate to other commuters on the road about the accidental stationed truck. Having gone through the entire records, it is evident that there are discrepancies in respect of the official version of exact time of the previous accident. ASI Kulbir Singh has been projected to be the eye witness of the subsequent accident. DD no.5A recorded the information about previous accident as mentioned in the charge sheet. Although DD no. 5A was not filed on record but same was called from police station concerned for its perusal to attain clarity of record. 
Statement u/s 161 Cr.PC of ASI Kulbir Singh forming part of the chargesheet records that DD no. 5A was assigned to him at about 12.00 midnight and that he had asked the respondent no.1 to remove the vehicle and also asked him to call for a crane to remove the said vehicle but the MACT No.
501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 10 of 31 directions were not complied by him. Bare perusal of DD no.5A shows that it was recorded at 2.54 A.M. It also records that the call was being made second time with no clarification as to the time of first call. It is obvious that first call was not responded with timely prompt and effective action which is why second call had to be made. 
Statement of R-1/Sadiq as recorded under section 161 Cr.PC mentions that his vehicle was rammed by another truck at about 02.00 AM while his complaint / Tehrir on the basis of which FIR no.99/19 was lodged, records the time of occurrence of offence at 01.00 AM. As per statement of ASI Kulbir Singh u/s 161 CrPC, he had instructed the driver of the offending vehicle to remove the vehicle whereas as per the status report/ clarification filed in writing upon queries by the Ld. Predecessor of this Court, he mentioned that the drivers of both the accidental vehicle Eicher Canter and Tata Truck were not present at the site when he reached at the spot of accident, having been assigned DD no. 5A and that he tried to indicate to the approaching vehicle by waiving his hand about the stationed truck, however, could not avert the accident. It is beyond comprehension as to how ASI Kulbir reached at the spot within two minutes of recording and assigning of DD entry, realized that the vehicles were in damaged condition and also made efforts to indicate to the other commuters about the stationed truck. There is no record as to when the first PCR call was made, if at all by R-1 or by driver of Tata Truck which was also parked ahead at roadside being damaged. The story being projected is that ASI Kulbir Singh did not have any time to respond to the emergency MACT No.
501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 11 of 31 and attempted measures within his control to avert any anticipated collision of vehicles resulting in further damage to life and property. As noted above, there are contradictions between the timing of the earlier accident, as officially recorded and also about the time when the information was given by R-1 or received by the police officials. It appears thus that there was considerable time gap between the earlier accident and the subsequent accident, however, timely measures were not taken to avert the same.
23. R-1 was the primary person who was incharge of the accidental vehicle, under an obligation towards safety of fellow commuters on a public road, who had a duty to ensure that his vehicle is Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
6 removed from a potentially offending location to a safer zone so as not to risk life of other road users. There is absolutely nothing in evidence to show that he attempted to use reflectors or any parking signs to indicate to other commuters about stationed truck in the middle of the road. ASI Kulbir Singh mentioned in the status report that driver of the offending vehicle was not present at the site when the subsequent accident happened. He also stated that he only found police officials to be present at the spot when he regained consciousness and that no private persons were present at the site. To say the least, it is in contradiction to the contents of the charge sheet in the present case and also prima facie with contents of FIR no. 99/2019.
24. What actually transpired at the site prior to accident in question can be revealed only by R-1 or by ASI Kulbir Singh who was assigned call of previous accident also. R-1 chose not to MACT No.
501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 12 of 31 adduce any evidence to show that he made all efforts to reach out the police officials and in the meanwhile to ensure indicating to other commuters about stationed damaged truck. R-1 being driver by profession, is expected to understand potential risk involved in leaving the vehicle unattended stationed on a dark road and the dangerous consequences that it might entail.
25. R-1 had made no attempt to negate the accusations made and chose not to even file reply to DAR to put across his version of the story. R-1 is a crucial link between the two accident and best person to explain the sequence of events post first accident, however, he chose not to enter the witness box. 
Insurance company also did not attempt to call R-1 as a witness so as to examine him about crucial missing details in the sole. 
26. There is thus nothing on record to suggest that any indications or precautions were taken by R-1 being solely responsible for the offending truck which led to subsequent collusion. 
27. Role of ASI Kulbir Singh is also dubious in the entire transaction. It is evident that ASI Kulbir Singh was assigned the previous call about damaged truck but he did not take any timely measure to get the damaged truck removed which led to subsequent collusion resulting in death of a person. It is also evident that measures were attempted only after the subsequent accident and in fact reporting of earlier accident was formalised and officially taken on record only because of involvement of accidental truck in yet another accident considering that DD no. 5A regarding previous accident was recorded at 02.54 AM MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No.
13 of 31 whereas GD entry for the subsequent collision which is subject matter of this case was recorded at 02.56 AM. Also injured Ankur Kushwaha mentioned that he found police officials present at the spot when he regained consciousness after few minutes of the accident but he has not testified about presence of any police officials prior to the accident near the truck as projected by ASI Kulbir Singh. There is no explanation as to why it was pitch dark on the main road even though it is apparent that it had extensive usage and movement of heavy vehicles. There is no investigation in to the aspect of installation and functionality of road lights either. 
28. He has explained as to how their bike was being run at a moderate speed and they could not have anticipated any stationary vehicle in the middle of the road. He also stated that they spotted the truck only ten seconds prior to the accident. Therefore, the deceased had practically no time to Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
7 understand, weigh and respond to the danger ahead and in no time, the collision happened. 
Although there was space on the left side of the offending truck on the road to negotiate through without a collision as testified by him, with relatively constricted space on the right side, the biker evidently attempted to overtake upon spotting the vehicle but failed since there was no space and also because of poor visibility on the road. 
29. The accident itself is not disputed. The manner of accident is also not disputed. Police authorities were immediately intimated. The identification of the offending vehicle or the driver thereof is also not disputed. It is settled that the vehicle MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . 
Page No. 14 of 31 need not be in motion to cause the accident. Negligence connotes lack of duty of care as expected from the reasonable person under the circumstance. There is no evidence that R-1 took any measures under his control despite being aware of dangerous consequences that his inaction could entail, in order to avert the accident. R-1 did not cross examine any of the witness. 
Even he did not file any reply to the DAR. 
30. After going through entire conspectus of case, perusal of evidence proved on record, criminal documents including charge sheet, it is evident that accident occurred due to negligence,
indifference and recklessness on the part of driver of offending vehicle. 
31. In view of the discussion, issue No. 1 is decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents. 
ii). Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 32. Section 168 MV Act enjoins the Claim Tribunals to hold an enquiry into the claim to make an effort determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable. Same is reproduced hereunder for ready reference:
"(1) Award of the Claims Tribunal.--On receipt of an application for compensation made under section 166 , the Claims Tribunal shall, after giving notice of the application to the insurer and after giving the parties (including the insurer) an opportunity of being heard, hold an inquiry into the claim or, as the case may be,
each of the claims and, subject to the provisions of section 162 may MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 15 of 31 make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and specifying the person or persons to whom compensation shall be paid and in making the award the Claims Tribunal shall specify the amount which shall be paid by the insurer or owner or driver of the vehicle involved in the accident or by all or any of them, as the case may be: Provided that where such application makes a claim for compensation under section 140 in respect of the death or permanent disablement of any person, such claim and any other claim (whether made in such application or otherwise) for compensation in respect of such death or permanent disablement shall be disposed of in accordance with the provisions of Chapter X. (2) The Claims Tribunal shall arrange to deliver Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
8 copies of the award to the parties concerned expeditiously and in any case within a period of fifteen days from the date of the award. (3) When an award is made under this section, the person who is required to pay any amount in terms of such award shall, within thirty days of the date of announcing the award by the Claims Tribunal,
deposit the entire amount awarded in such manner as the Claims Tribunal may direct." 
33. Before putting in frame the position of law, it is noted that the process of determining the compensation by the court is essentially a very difficult task and can never be an exact science. 
Perfect compensation is hardly possible, more so in claims of injury and disability. (As observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sidram Vs. The Divisional Manager United India Insurance Company Ltd, SLP (Civil) No. 19277 of 2019). 
34 The basic principle in assessing motor vehicle MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 16 of 31 compensation claims, is to place the victim in as near a position as she or he was in before the accident, with other compensatory directions for loss of amenities and other payments. 
These general principles have been stated and reiterated in several decisions. [Support drawn from Govind Yadav v. New India Insurance Co. Ltd., (2011) 10 SCC 683] . 
35. This Tribunal has been tasked with determination of just compensation. The observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Divisional Controller, KSRTC v. Mahadeva Shetty and Another,
(2003) 7 SCC 197, needs mention here (para 15): 
"Statutory provisions clearly indicate that the compensation must be "just" and it cannot be a bonanza; not a source of profit but the same should not be a pittance. The courts and tribunals have a duty to weigh the various factors and quantify the amount of compensation, which should be just. What would be "just" compensation is a vexed question. There can be no golden rule applicable to all cases for measuring the value of human life or a limb. Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precise mathematical calculations. It would depend upon the particular facts and circumstances, and attending peculiar or special features, if any. Every method or mode adopted for assessing compensation has to be considered in the background of "just" compensation which is the pivotal consideration. Though by use of the expression "which appears to it to be just", a wide discretion is vested in the Tribunal,
the determination has to be rational, to be done by a judicious approach and not the outcome of whims, wild guesses and arbitrariness.. ..." 
36. Delineating the damages as pecuniary and non pecuniary, MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik &
Anr. . Page No. 17 of 31 Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case of R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt Ltd, 1995 AIR 755, made following observations:
"9....while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.
Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which are Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
9 capable of being calculated in terms of money; whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations. In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial;
(iii) other material loss. So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e., on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, hardship, discomfort, disappointment, frustration and mental stress in life." 
37. Certain principles for delineating just compensation were enumerated in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Following observations are relevant in the context:
"40.General principles relating to compensation in injury cases MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. . Page No. 18 of 31 5. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. [See C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 :
1995 SCC (Cri) 250] and Baker v. Willoughby [1970 AC 467 : (1970) 2 WLR 50 :
(1969) 3 All ER 1528 (HL)] .]
6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: 
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
Ankur Kushwaha (Dar) vs Saddik (100/19, Srv) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128464702/
10 (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of MACT No. 501/19 Ankur Vs. Saddik & Anr. .
Page No. 19 of 31 permanent disability. 
(iii) Future medical expenses. 
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv).
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 
7. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 
Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 
Assessment of non-pecuniary damages-- Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury/deprivation/ disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. Decisions of this Court and the High Courts contain necessary guidelines for award under these heads, if necessary.
